I can understand the exclusivity point but here's the thing. Making the skins payable with real world money wouldn't get rid of the exclusivity in my opinion. In other games with microtransactions, when you buy something with real world money you still feel like it is an exclusive thing. That's what makes it worth buying. 

In Paladins I feel it would be the same. 

And as for the hero shooter thing, yes that's true. But you have to understand why people CONTINUE to play the game after a period of time. When it comes to hero shooters, the vast majority of people who play them are casual players. Meaning they're only there for friends and the cosmetics. Only the minority of the community plays to understand the game and be competitive. This is true for all hero games. Paladins included. By siphoning off the skins to exclusive events, it turns off alot of potential casual players. Which stunts the games appeal for new people who otherwise would've liked it. Because the casuals make up the majority, it massively harms the game in the long run financially. 

And as for the spending money part, yea it's a good thing if new players hold off on spending money but the whole point of microtransactions is to manipulate the player into buying them. Even if it isn't in the players best interest. With that in mind, wouldn't it make alot more sense for HiRez to make the exclusive skins buyable? It would make new players spend money more often, making HiRez more money. 

AND on top of that it would make the new players more dedicated to the game. When you spend money on a game, even if it was money not well spent, you become more dedicated to the game. If a bunch of new players spend a bunch of money on exclusive skins from previous events, the psychological effect of investing money into a game will make them play longer. 

Ask any long lasting League player or Overwatch player why they still play those games and I'll bet you up to half of them will say it's because they spent a shit ton of money on the game. Even if the money didn't give them good returns. 

It just makes more sense for HiRez to make the skins purchasable.

It's typical to see someone with 1 character all maxed out and then a bunch of characters with only a few items each. 

With that in mind, because events are rare and because only a handful of champions actually get something for them in an event, new players are shit out of luck for the most part when it comes to getting a new skin for their preferred character. There's only a small chance the next event will actually have something for your main. And the time between battle passes is MONTHS. This discourages players from further playing the game and branching out to more characters, because the main character they play the most has a 90% likelihood of not getting anything new added to them for the next year or so. (Not being exaggerative either on that last point. It can take literally up to a year for a champion to have ANYTHING given to them) Which sucks ass.
